title: Field with its own contract: seen factor, second-order terms, fall and clock

key_results.statement: Class: every member of $\mathcal D$ and every nondegenerate eigenvector $\varphi_0$ of $C_f$, $\varepsilon=0$ or $\varepsilon>0$; regime: none (R0); status: exact. $\hat C=\hat C_b\otimes\mathbb 1_c+\sum_xP_x\otimes\kappa xX$ with $\hat C_b=A+\sum_xP_x\otimes[N(x)\sigma_3\otimes(m+D)+e_0]$, the member of $\mathcal C$ with $\zeta_x=1$, $m_x=mN(x)$, $\eta_x=N(x)$, $V_x=e_0$; $\hat C$ is the contract of an admissible description of $b$ and $c$.

Class $\mathcal D$, R0, exact: under (2.20) $N(x)\to N(x)+a_x$, $e_0\to e_0+c$, while $\varphi_0$, $\tilde\Phi_x$, $S$, $\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f$, $\nu$ and $\hat C$ are unchanged; $N(x)$ is well defined only together with the coefficient of $B_x$ in $C_{br}$ (zero in the form of $\mathcal D$).
Class $\mathcal D$, every start of the body, no condition on $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$; status: bound, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda$.

Class $\mathcal D$; regime R1: $2\epsilon_1+2\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3<1$ with $\epsilon_3=\nu M_{\max}/\Delta_f$, weak records (a sufficient condition for the construction, not shown to be necessary); status: order estimate of the constant, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le2\epsilon_1[1+O(\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)]$; for $\varepsilon=0$ the left side is zero for every $\nu$ and $\epsilon_2$.

Class $\mathcal D$, every schedule of readings on $b$ and $c$: bound $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert\le2\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda_k$ for all $\lambda_k\ge0$ without conditions; in R1 (order estimate, fixed schedule) $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert=O(\epsilon_1^2)+O(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f\lambda_k)$, so the statistics are those of a sharp field with profile $N(x)$ through first order in $\epsilon_1$ on $\lambda\ll1/(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f)$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1: $H_{\rm eff}=\hat C-\tfrac12(\mathcal S_1^{\dagger}W_1+W_1^{\dagger}\mathcal S_1)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$ with $\mathcal S_1$ the solution of the Sylvester equation; for the exact $H_{\rm eff}$, $\lVert\Pi_0\Psi(\lambda)-(e^{-iH_{\rm eff}\lambda}(\phi\otimes\chi))\otimes\varphi_0\rVert\le2\epsilon_1^2[1+\dots]$ for all $\lambda\ge0$ (order estimate of the constant); a truncation $H'$ adds at most $\lambda\lVert H_{\rm eff}-H'\rVert$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact coefficient of the second order in $\epsilon_1$ at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: $H^{(2)}=-\sum_x\gamma_xP_x\otimes\mathbb 1_2\otimes(m+D)^2\otimes\mathbb 1_c$ with $\gamma_x=\langle\varphi_0\vert\tilde\Phi_xS\tilde\Phi_x\vert\varphi_0\rangle$, $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert\le\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_f$, $\lVert H^{(2)}\rVert\le\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact first corrections with an order estimate of the remainder $O(\epsilon_1^2(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2\Delta_f)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$: $H^{(2,1)}=-\tfrac\tau2\sum_x(c_xh_x\otimes(-i\sigma_1)+c_x^{*}h_x^{\dagger}\otimes(i\sigma_1))\otimes\mathcal M^2$ with $c_x=\tfrac12(\rho_{xx}+\rho_{x+1,x+1})+\rho_{x+1,x}$, and $H^{(3)}=\sum_x\gamma^{(3)}_xP_x\otimes\sigma_3\otimes\mathcal M^3$; $\lVert H^{(2,1)}\rVert\le2\tau\epsilon_1^2$, $\lVert H^{(3)}\rVert\le\epsilon_1^2\epsilon_3\Delta_f$; $\hat C+H^{(2)}$ reproduces the statistics to accuracy $\eta\gg\epsilon_1^2$ for $\lambda\lesssim\eta/[\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3+\epsilon_1^2)]$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with first corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: on the level $k$ the on-site block is $(N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3)\sigma_3+(e_0-\gamma_xM_k^2)\mathbb 1_2$ and the hopping block is $-\tfrac{i\tau}2(1-M_k^2c_x)\sigma_1$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the body part of $\hat C+H^{(2)}$ is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ for every member of $\mathcal D$ ($M_{x,k}=N(x)M_k>0$), and of $\mathcal C$ iff $\gamma_x=0$ for all $x$; with the first corrections it is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ up to the hopping phase (present iff $\operatorname{Im}\rho_{x+1,x}\neq0$) if and only if the condition (P) of (10.27) holds; a unitary $U$ diagonal in $(x,s,k)$ removes the phase from the contract and acts on the start, so the position and branch statistics with the phase and the start $\phi$ are those without the phase and the start $U^{\dagger}\phi$, which differs from $\phi$ also for a start in one level; all new terms are well defined under (2.20).

Class: linear profiles $\Phi_x=N_0+xY$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$; status: closed forms of the level data of the body part of $H_{\rm eff}$: $\tau_k=\tau(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)$, $\hat M_k=M_k(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)$, $G_k=gM_k+\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^3$, $\mathcal F_k=\gamma_1M_k^2$, $g_{\zeta,k}=-4M_k^2\operatorname{Re}\rho_Y$, $V_k=e_0-\gamma_0M_k^2$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ they are level data of a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ for the whole class, with the first corrections only under (10.28); at leading order in $\kappa$ the body evolves by the effective body contract, whose plain gradient is $\mathcal F_k-\kappa\langle X\rangle$; a level offset is a common phase for a start in one level.

Class: linear profiles of the field, branch starts at rest; condition $\langle X\rangle=0$ (for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ see (10.22)); regime R1 as in (10.12); status: closed form with remainder $O(\varepsilon^4)$ and second corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]$ with $\beta=g(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)-\gamma^{(3)}_1$, $\lvert\gamma_1\rvert M_k\le2\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_YM_{\max}/\Delta_f$, $\rho_0M_k^2\le\epsilon_1^2$; the leading term in $\gamma_1$ holds for the whole class, the term in $\beta$ under (10.28).

Class and regime of (10.13), condition $\langle X\rangle=0$ (for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ see (10.23)), exact at the stated order: at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and every $N\ge2$, level-independence of $a_{k,+}(0)$, of $a_{k,-}(0)$ and of both with one value $-\tau^2g$ each hold iff $\gamma_1=0$; with the first corrections, under (10.28), for $N\ge3$ iff $\gamma_1=0$ and $\beta=0$, for $N=2$ upper iff $\gamma_1+\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, lower iff $\gamma_1-\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, both iff $\gamma_1=\beta=0$; the independence is lost at order $\epsilon_1^2$, leading order in $\epsilon_2$.

Class: every member of $\mathcal D$ and every $x$ (it follows from (10.11)); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ plus the first correction in $\epsilon_3$ (no term of first order in $\epsilon_2$); status: closed form: $E^+_{x,k+1}-E^+_{x,k}=\frac{2\pi}{N\lambda_0}[N(x)-\gamma_x(M_k+M_{k+1})+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_k^2+M_kM_{k+1}+M_{k+1}^2)]$; $E^+_{x,k}$ is the on-site eigenvalue of the branch place $s=1$, the upper one at leading order for every member and with the cubic term iff $N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3>0$.

Class: linear profiles, starts $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$, every member; regime R1 at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ only (description with $\hat C+H^{(2)}$) and at the orders of (3.36); status: order estimate: the clock statistics is the ring-clock mixture (3.36) with every advance shifted by $-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma\lambda/\lambda_0$ (rate $\bar r(x_0)=[N(x_0)-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma]/\lambda_0$ in the wide-start limit) up to total variation $\le\tfrac12\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2\lambda$, so to accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2)$ if $N\ge3$ and $\gamma_{x_0}\neq0$; for $N=2$ or $\gamma_{x_0}=0$ there is no deviation at this order, and the range is then set by (10.30) and (10.10), not all $\lambda$.

Class: linear profiles, every member (no condition (10.28) at this order); condition $\langle X\rangle=0$ (for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ see (10.26)); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$; status: closed form of the leading defect: with $\bar r(x)=[N(x)-\gamma_x\Sigma]/\lambda_0$, $\mathcal R_k=a_{k,+}(0)+\tau^2(\bar r(x+1)-\bar r(x))/\bar r(x)=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma]$, $\Sigma=M_0+M_{N-1}$; the relation (4.24) holds for all levels iff $\gamma_1=0$ and $g\gamma_0=0$.

Class: independent cells, every $\Delta_x>0$, $n_x>0$, $\varepsilon_x\ge0$; regime R1 with $\epsilon_3=\epsilon_1$; status: exact evaluation of the coefficients: $N(x)=n_x$, $\varepsilon=\max_x\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f=\min_x\Delta_x$, $\gamma_x=\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$, $\rho_{xy}=\delta_{xy}\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2$, $c_x=\tfrac12(\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2+\varepsilon_{x+1}^2/\Delta_{x+1}^2)$, $\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$; the body part of $H_{\rm eff}$ is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ for every cell description, with level profiles that depend on $x$ in a general way: $M_{x,k}=n_xM_k>0$ (the condition (P) holds without a condition) and $1-M_k^2c_x\ge1-\epsilon_1^2>0$.

Class: one cell with the body at $x$, branch sign $\pm$, level $k$; status: exact: the cell contract $C_{f_x}\pm M_k\Phi_x$ has the lower eigenvalue $\pm M_kn_x-\Omega_{x,k}$ and the upper eigenvalue $\pm M_kn_x+\Omega_{x,k}$ with $\Omega_{x,k}=\sqrt{\Delta_x^2/4+M_k^2\varepsilon_x^2}$; overlap of the lower eigenvector with the cell start $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)=[\tfrac12(1+\Delta_x/2\Omega_{x,k})]^{1/2}$; at leading order in $\tau/\Delta_x$ the hopping block is multiplied by $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)\cos(\alpha_{x+1,k}/2)$.

Class: only the cells of the subclass $\mathcal L$ of (10.31) (linear level profiles, an assumption of this package), branch starts at rest; condition $\langle X\rangle=0$ (for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ the record term $-\sigma\tau^2\kappa\langle X\rangle[1/M_k-2\rho_0M_k]$ of (10.22) is added); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first order in the gradients $g$, $\gamma_1$, $\rho_1$ of the cell data; status: closed form: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+2g\rho_0M_k^2]$ with $\gamma_1=\varepsilon_{x+1}^2/\Delta_{x+1}-\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$ the same for all $x$ and $\rho_0=\tfrac12(c_{-1}+c_0)$; control within $\mathcal L$, $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$ constant: the branch-odd term vanishes, while the level offsets, the defect $\tau^2g\gamma\Sigma$ of (4.24) and the level-dependent hopping remain; for cells outside $\mathcal L$ the quoted inputs do not determine the fall, the defect of (4.24) and the clock range.

Class $\mathcal D$ (linear profiles for fall, clock, relation and velocity), regime R1, every $\langle X\rangle$, status: order estimate: the factor seen, the level-independence of the fall from rest, the one-rate ring clock and the relation (4.24) are unchanged by a field with its own contract at order $\epsilon_1$ and first change at order $\epsilon_1^2$ at the leading order of the coefficient in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, with relative size $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert M_{\max}\le\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f/M_{\max}$; the velocity of a branch start at rest from the hopping phase first appears at order $\epsilon_1^2$ and first order in $\epsilon_2$.

Class: linear profiles of the field, branch starts at rest, every $\langle X\rangle$; regime R1 as in (10.12), leading order in $\kappa$ in the convention of 04-branch-fall (effective body contract, plain gradient $-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ kept); status: closed form as (10.13): $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]+a^{\rm rec}_{k,\sigma}$ with $a^{\rm rec}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\tau_k^2\kappa\langle X\rangle/\hat M_k=-\sigma\tau^2\kappa\langle X\rangle[1/M_k-(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)M_k]$; the terms in $\beta$, $\rho_0$, $\gamma^{(3)}_0$ hold under (10.28), the others for the whole class; the record term is of zeroth order in $\epsilon_1$, odd in the branch and different for every two levels, of relative size $\kappa\lvert\langle X\rangle\rvert/(\lvert g\rvert M_k)$ against $-\tau^2g$ and $\kappa\lvert\langle X\rangle\rvert/(\lvert\gamma_1\rvert M_k^2)$ against $\sigma\tau^2\gamma_1M_k$.

Class and regime of (10.22), case $\langle X\rangle\neq0$, exact at the stated order, with $\gamma_1'=\gamma_1+\kappa\langle X\rangle(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)$: at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the fall from rest is level-dependent in each branch for $N\ge3$, and for $N=2$ level-independent in the upper branch iff $\gamma_1M_0M_1=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ iff in the lower branch, with the two values $\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1(M_0+M_1)]$; with the first corrections, under (10.28), it is level-dependent in each branch for $N\ge4$, level-independent in the branch $\sigma$ for $N=3$ iff $\sigma\kappa\langle X\rangle=\beta M_0M_1M_2$ and $\sigma\gamma_1'=-\beta(M_0+M_1+M_2)$, and for $N=2$ iff $\gamma_1'+\kappa\langle X\rangle/(M_0M_1)+\sigma\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$; for every $N\ge2$ independence in both branches with one value implies $\langle X\rangle=0$.

Class: linear profiles of the field, branch starts $B_{k,\sigma}[g]$, every $\langle X\rangle$, under (10.28); regime R1, zero gradients with the uniform hopping phase $\theta_k=M_k^2\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$ kept, first order in $\theta_k$, infinite chain; status: exact coefficient in the description with $H_{\rm eff}$, derived from the velocity operator $-\tau_k\cos(p-\theta_k)\sigma_1$ of the level block: $\mathrm d\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)$ with $v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\sigma\theta_k\langle\omega_k''-\tau^2M_k^2\cos^2p\,\omega_k^{-3}\cos(2\omega_k\lambda)\rangle_g$, $\lvert\rho_Y\rvert\le\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_Y/\Delta_f^2$; it is bounded in $\lambda$, so the drift accelerations (10.13), (10.22) are unchanged at first order in $Y$.

Class: linear profiles of the field, branch starts at rest, under (10.28); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first order in $\epsilon_2$ (no term in $\epsilon_3$), first order in $Y$; status: exact coefficient in the description with $H_{\rm eff}$; a velocity, not a drift acceleration: with the sharp label at fixed $\lambda$, $v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\sigma\tau^2M_k\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y[1-\cos(2M_k\lambda)]$; averaged over a long window, before or after the sharp label, $\bar v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\tau^2M_k\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$ with $\lvert\bar v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}\rvert\le\tau^2M_k\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_Y/\Delta_f^2$; the limits $\lambda\to\infty$ and sharp label do not commute for the velocity itself; it is odd in the branch, different for every two levels, and vanishes iff $\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y=0$.

Class: linear profiles, every member, every $\langle X\rangle$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$, leading order in $\kappa$ with the plain gradient kept; status: closed form of the leading defect: $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k]$; for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ the relation (4.24) fails already at zeroth order in $\epsilon_1$; it holds for all levels iff $\gamma_1=0$, $g\gamma_0=0$ and $\langle X\rangle=0$ for $N\ge3$, and iff $g\gamma_0=0$ and $\gamma_1M_0M_1=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ for $N=2$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1: with $\mu_{x,k}=N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3$, the body part of $\hat C+H^{(2)}+H^{(2,1)}+H^{(3)}$ is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ up to the hopping phase if and only if (P): $\mu_{x,k}>0$ for all $x,k$; margin (P') against the remainder of (10.10): $\min_{x,k}\mu_{x,k}\gg\epsilon_1^2[(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2+\epsilon_1^2]\Delta_f$; since $\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_x\rvert M_k^2\le\varepsilon\epsilon_1\epsilon_3$, the condition $\varepsilon\epsilon_1\epsilon_3<\min_xN(x)$ is sufficient for (P); R1 does not imply (P): for $C_f=\Delta\lvert1\rangle\langle1\rvert$, $\varphi_0=\lvert0\rangle$, $\Phi_x=n+v(\lvert0\rangle\langle1\rvert+\lvert1\rangle\langle0\rvert)+a\lvert1\rangle\langle1\rvert$ with $a<0$ and $0<n<\lvert a\rvert v^2M_0^2/\Delta^2$ all $\mu_{x,k}$ are negative; where $\mu_{x,k}<0$ the class condition fails, the upper on-site eigenvalue is $V_{x,k}-\mu_{x,k}$ with the branch place $s=2$, and $V_{x,k}+\mu_{x,k}$ is the lower one.

Class: linear profiles of the field, regime R1, first corrections: the level data (10.12) are those of a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ on the chain $\lvert x\rvert\le L$ if and only if $\hat M_k>\lvert G_k\rvert L$, that is $1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2>\lvert g+\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^2\rvert L$, and $\lvert g_{\zeta,k}\rvert(L-\tfrac12)<1$ for all $k$ ($\tau_k>0$ holds in R1); margins: $(\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_0\rvert+\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_1\rvert L)M_{\max}^2\ll1-\lvert g\rvert L$ (sufficient for the first relation and for the expansion of $1/\hat M_k$) and $M_0(1-\lvert g\rvert L)\gg\epsilon_1^2[(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2+\epsilon_1^2]\Delta_f$; $8\epsilon_1^2<1$ is sufficient for the relation on $g_{\zeta,k}$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the inequalities hold for the whole class; R1 does not imply (10.28), and the statements with the first corrections are not derived for members in which it fails.

Class: every member of $\mathcal D$, every $x$, regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$: $E^+_{x,k+2}-2E^+_{x,k+1}+E^+_{x,k}=2(2\pi/N\lambda_0)^2[-\gamma_x+3\gamma^{(3)}_xM_{k+1}]$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the differences (10.15) are independent of $k$ iff $N=2$ or $\gamma_x=0$; with the first corrections iff $N=2$, or $N=3$ and $\gamma_x=3\gamma^{(3)}_xM_1$, or $N\ge4$ and $\gamma_x=\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$; a member with $\gamma_x=0\neq\gamma^{(3)}_x$ has equal differences at leading order and unequal ones with the first corrections for every $N\ge3$.

Class: linear profiles of the field, starts $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$, under (10.28); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with the first correction in $\epsilon_3$, zeroth order in the gradients, wide-start limit at fixed $\lambda$, on the range of (10.10); status: order estimate: $\bar r(x)=\lambda_0^{-1}[N(x)-\gamma_x\Sigma+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_0^2+M_0M_{N-1}+M_{N-1}^2)]$, the levels deviate from a ring clock with the rate $\bar r(x_0)$ by $\delta E_k=d_k(d_{N-1}-d_k)[\gamma_{x_0}-\gamma^{(3)}_{x_0}(M_k+\Sigma)]$, and with $\Xi_{x_0}=\max_{0<k<N-1}\lvert\gamma_{x_0}-\gamma^{(3)}_{x_0}(M_k+\Sigma)\rvert\le\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert+3\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_{x_0}\rvert M_{\max}$ the total variation from the ring clock is $\le\tfrac12\Xi_{x_0}d_{N-1}^2\lambda$, so accuracy $\eta$ holds for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\Xi_{x_0}d_{N-1}^2)$; the spacings impose no restriction iff $N=2$ or $\Xi_{x_0}=0$ (the equal-spacing cases of (10.29)), and the range is then that of (10.10), not all $\lambda$; the cubic term adds at most $\tfrac32\epsilon_1^2\epsilon_3\Delta_f(d_{N-1}/M_{\max})^2\lambda$.

Subclass $\mathcal L$ of the cells, an assumption of this package: $n_x=1+gx$, $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x=\gamma_0+\gamma_1x$ and $c_x=\tfrac12(\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2+\varepsilon_{x+1}^2/\Delta_{x+1}^2)=\rho_0+\rho_1(x+\tfrac12)$ for all $x$ of the chain; for cells with $n_x=1+gx$ it holds if and only if the level profiles of the body part are linear for all levels, and it is not implied by $n_x=1+gx$ (for example $\Delta_x=\Delta$, $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta=\gamma_0+\delta(-1)^x$ is outside $\mathcal L$); first order in the gradients of the cell data means first order jointly in $g$, $\gamma_1$, $\rho_1$ in the sense of 04-branch-fall.

open_issues: (10.6), the R1 part of (10.7) and the remainders of (10.10) are order estimates: their constants and the dependence of (10.7) on the number of readings are not bounded explicitly.

The accelerations (10.13), (10.20), (10.22) and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) are those of the description with H_eff; for the description with C only the agreement of the statistics within (10.10) is derived, not a statement about its acceleration or its velocity.

Members in which the positive rest term condition (P) of (10.27), or (10.28) for the linear profiles, fails or holds without its margin: the statements with the first corrections are not derived for them; the exchange of the branch places of a level with a negative rest term is named but not worked out, and a rest term that changes sign along the chain is not treated.

Item 4(c) is answered for the subclass L of (10.31) only; for cells with n_x = 1 + g x whose γ_x or c_x is not linear in x (for example an alternating ε_x²/Δ_x) the fall from rest, the defect of (4.24) and the clock range are not determined by the quoted inputs and need a result for level profiles that are not linear.

(10.16) has the orders of (3.36), zeroth order in the gradients, and the leading order in ε2, ε3; (10.30) holds in the wide-start limit only; the loss of clock coherence by the level-dependent force and by the level-dependent velocity (10.25), which separate the levels in position at first order in the gradients, is not treated.

For profiles of the field that are not linear the phase of the hopping depends on x; its effect is given only as the change of the start of Step 2(b), and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) is derived for the linear profiles.

Where 2ε1 + 2ε2 + ε3 ≥ 1 (a slow field, or ε3 not small) the norm estimates of this package do not control the expansion and only (10.1), (10.2), (10.4) and the first part of (10.7) are derived; whether an effective description exists there is not determined, except for ε = 0, where it is exact.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: γ_x is an inverse cost, γ_x·M_k² a cost, ρ·M_k², γ1·M_k and β·M_k² pure numbers like g, accelerations τ² times a number as in (4.16); κ⟨X⟩/M_k is a pure number, the hopping phase θ_k is a pure number and the velocity τ²·M_k·ρ_Y is a cost, the dimension of a rate of the position label; the rest term μ_{x,k} is a cost and Ξ·d²·λ a pure number.

Sharp field ε = 0: all new coefficients vanish, H_eff equals the compression, the excited component is zero and (2.3) is recovered; field operators commuting with C_f force ε = 0; (10.22) reduces to (4.16) for the variant (a) with the plain gradient −κ⟨X⟩, level-independent iff ⟨X⟩ = 0 as (4.22) states, and the velocity (10.25) vanishes; the conditions (P) and (10.28) hold and Ξ = 0.

Exact on-site problems against the expansion: for a cell the exact lower eigenvalue and overlap reproduce the second-order on-site term, the vanishing third-order term and the hopping factor; for the two-place field of Step 2(b) the branch-odd part of the exact lower eigenvalue at second order in v, n·M + a·v²·M³/(Δ² − M²a²), reproduces the rest term μ with the third-order coefficient and its negative sign for a < 0 and small n.
